text: Emily Chen: Heads-up we have a product request to refine the trial notice that appears in-app. It's a compact banner on the dashboard and a larger modal on usage spike. Need microcopy recs that work across both. Current banner: 'Trial ends in 7 days. Upgrade to keep access.' Modal: 'Your trial will end soon. Upgrade now to avoid service interruption.' Both feel a bit heavy. Thoughts? Jordan Park: Agree, modal language is too alarming. For modal we can be slightly more descriptive: 'Your free trial ends in 7 days. Choose a plan to keep access and billing options.' But that might be too wordy. Samir Patel: For the banner, short and scannable wins. Options: '7 days left on your trial' or '7 days left Consider upgrading'. Keep CTA explicit. Ava Lopez: Marketing prefers positive framing: 'Keep building with Redwood Upgrade before your trial ends' vs 'Your trial ends'. Tests have shown 'Keep building' converts better for dev audiences. Olga Kuznetsova: Accessibility: banner should use aria-live="polite" and the modal aria-live="assertive". Also, CTAs must have descriptive accessible names: avoid bare verbs like 'Upgrade'. Use 'Upgrade plan' or 'Choose a plan'. If a secondary action is 'Remind me', include a clear accessible label: 'Remind me later snooze trial notice'. Rohit Desai: Dev constraints: mobile banner truncates at 48 chars; modal title field limited to 60 chars. Also need pluralization in i18n: keys like `trial.notice.days_left` with variants for zero/one/many. Example: `{{count}} day left` vs `{{count}} days left`. Emily Chen: Let's propose specific strings for the two surfaces and the expired state. Drafts: - Banner (short): "{{days}} days left Keep building Upgrade plan" (CTA text: "Upgrade plan") - Banner (direct): "{{days}} days left on your trial View plans" (CTA: "View plans") - Modal (friendly): "Your free trial ends in {{days}} days" + body: "Keep access to your projects by choosing a plan. Billing options are available.", CTA: "Choose a plan" secondary: "Remind me in 3 days" - Expired: Title: "Your trial has ended" body: "Your workspace is in read-only mode. Choose a plan to restore write access." CTA: "View billing options" Which of these should be our A variant vs B? Jordan Park: A/B suggestion: Banner A = short keep-building (friendly), Banner B = direct days-left (explicit). Modal: always use friendly copy but with clear CTAs. We should also test CTA label variants: 'Upgrade plan' vs 'Choose a plan'. Samir Patel: UI notes: in the modal, put the CTA on the right and the secondary on the left. For banners, put an unobtrusive clock icon on the left; keep contrast accessible. Olga Kuznetsova: For SR users, add hidden context: aria-describedby pointing to a hidden element that contains full sentence including the CTA purpose, e.g., 'Opens billing page'. Eg: `` and hidden div id="trial-billing-desc">Opens billing settings to upgrade your plan. Also ensure focus management when the modal appears (focus trap + announcement). Rohit Desai: I'll make sure i18n keys include full strings for aria-labels separate from visible copy: `trial.banner.cta.visible` and `trial.banner.cta.aria` so we can keep visible short and accessible label verbose. Also will add fallback behavior for small viewports to swap CTA text to the shorter variant. Ava Lopez: Tone approval: marketing prefers 'Keep building' hero language in banner A and 'Choose a plan' CTA in the modal. They want to review the exact phrasing for other locales. Emily Chen: Action items: Jordan to prepare Figma frames for A/B (frames for banner A/B + modal), Rohit to add i18n keys and mobile fallback, Olga to add accessibility checklist for this component, Ava to coordinate marketing review. I'll add the final strings to the PR once frames are attached. ops-bot: Created task INFR-1297 for rollout to 10% of users, feature flag: trial_notice_v2. Jordan Park: I'll post Figma link in the PR and tag everyone. Quick note for copy: prefer 'Choose a plan' over 'Upgrade' for clarity when users are on a free tier vs trial. Emily Chen: Thanks! Planning to land copy patch today. If anyone sees a clear problem with the phrasing, reply here before EOD. :white_check_mark:
